key_insight: The paper argues that turbulent coherent structures are universal thermodynamic responses to macroscopic energy-throughput imbalance, and introduces an effective order parameter (Π) to classify them within a non-equilibrium framework.
engineering_relevance: This could provide a principled way to decide when CFD must resolve coherent structures versus when they can be treated as transient fluctuations, improving model fidelity and mesh/closure choices.
method: Renormalized Navier–Stokes equations are used to connect turbulence with non-equilibrium statistical physics.
Coherent structures are interpreted through bifurcation accessibility: near-equilibrium fluctuation-like vs far-from-equilibrium dissipative states.
An effective thermodynamic order parameter (Π) is proposed for identifying flow organization and resolution needs.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical framework and claims computability of Π, but it does not report numerical experiments, benchmarks, or validation datasets.
watch_item: The framework’s practical value will depend on how robustly Π can be computed and validated across different turbulent flows and numerical discretizations.
paper_title: Coherence as Thermodynamic Organization: Toward a Non-Equilibrium Turbulence Theory
